questions.question_text:
The curve $y=-2^{x}+16$ cuts the $x$-axis.
Find the $x$-intercept.

options.why: Read the constant $16$ as the intercept instead of solving $2^{x}=16$.
Halved $16$ instead of finding the power of $2$ equal to $16$.
Used $2^{3}=8$; but $2^{4}=16$ is needed.
$2^{x}$ increases, but the shown graph decreases from left to right.
This has $y$-intercept $1$ and drops below the asymptote, not $y$-intercept $3$.
Correct decay shape but its asymptote is $y=-2$, not $y=2$.

questions.solution_text:
Decreasing means a $-x$ exponent (reflection in the $y$-axis); asymptote $y=2$ means $c=2$; $y$-intercept $2^{0}+2=3$ checks.
$y=2^{-x}+2$
